query: Write me a systemd service and timer pair that runs /usr/local/bin/nightly-backup every night at 2:00 local time, and say where each file goes.
result:
Both files are system units, so they go in `/etc/systemd/system/`. Your dotfiles rule says `/etc` changes land first in `~/.dotfiles/bluefin/etc/systemd/system/`, so the source copies live there and are installed from there.

`nightly-backup.service`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nightly-backup
NoNewPrivileges=yes
PrivateTmp=yes
ProtectSystem=strict
ReadWritePaths=/var/backups
```

`nightly-backup.timer`:

```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run nightly-backup at 02:00

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 02:00:00
RandomizedDelaySec=1min
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

The service has no `[Install]` section because the timer starts it. `Persistent=true` runs a missed backup at the next boot, for example if the desktop was off at 2:00. `RandomizedDelaySec=1min` can push the start up to a minute past 2:00. Set it to `0` if you want exact timing.

I don't know what `nightly-backup` writes to, so `ReadWritePaths=/var/backups` is a guess. Under `ProtectSystem=strict` the whole filesystem is read-only except that path. Replace it with the script's real destination. The directory must exist before the unit starts, or startup fails with a mount namespacing error. If the script reads under `/home`, check that nothing else blocks it.

To install, copy both files to `/etc/systemd/system/`, then run:

```
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now nightly-backup.timer
systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/nightly-backup.{service,timer}
```
